text:
maria: Heads up — multiple customers reporting TLS cert warnings for model-api.redwood.ai starting ~07:05 UTC. Intermittent: some connections get the wildcard cert (*.redwood-edge.net) and browsers show mismatch. This started right after the egress NAT change. Anyone seeing weird SNI values in ALB logs?

jon: I see spikes in ALB logs with SNI = "-" and a bunch of 495-like entries. Curious if the client_hello is missing SNI on those flows.

patrick: Can you paste a raw ALB access log line? I ran into similar behavior when a proxy was doing SSL bumping recently.

maria: here's a sanitized excerpt from ALB logs around 07:06: 
```
https 2026-03-18T07:06:11.123Z app/alb 10.0.1.5:443 54.12.34.56:12345 0.000 0.001 0.000 200 495 0 57 "GET https://model-api.redwood.ai/health HTTP/1.1" "curl/7.79.1" TLSv1.3 ECDHE... - -
```
(Notice the "-" where SNI should be.)

maria: Our deployment change replaced the NAT instance with an egress-proxy cluster (haproxy/squid) at ~07:00 UTC. Suspect the proxy is touching TLS.

cheng: HAProxy doesn't rewrite SNI unless it's terminating TLS. Did we enable ssl_fc_sni inspect or ssl_preread and then do backend routing? infra-bot: rollout egress-proxy v2 at 07:00 UTC by rollout-bot.

jon: I grabbed a tcpdump from one of the egress IPs — some ClientHello frames show empty SNI. Not all clients, only a subset. Could be a broken client, or our proxy munging the client_hello for multiplexing.

patrick: Do we have any transparent TLS interception (SSL bump) rules in squid? That would generate a new ClientHello toward the ALB and could set SNI to the upstream host configured (or blank).

maria: config snippet from haproxy we pushed: 
```
frontend fe-443
  bind *:443
  mode tcp
  option tcplog
  tcp-request inspect-delay 5s
  tcp-request content accept if { req_ssl_hello_type 1 }
  use_backend be-models if { req_ssl_sni -m end model-api.redwood.ai }
```
We added a fallback to wildcard backend which has the *.redwood-edge.net cert. If req_ssl_sni matching fails (e.g., empty SNI), it falls back to wildcard backend.

cheng: using `-m end` is fragile — it fails on subtle variants (trailing dot, punycode differences). Also when SNI is empty the ACL doesn't match and you hit default. We should switch to `-m dom` or regex and explicitly check for empty SNI.

jon: immediate mitigation: rolled back the egress-proxy cluster to the previous NAT instance at 07:20 UTC. Alerts dropped ~90% afterwards. Still seeing a small tail (cached connections).

sre-oncall: Incident created. Added a metric to watch ALB lines with SNI == "-" per minute and an alert: >5/min for 5m. Oncall monitoring for next 2 hrs.

patrick: Post-incident actions I propose: 1) Adjust HAProxy ACL to explicitly detect empty SNI and route to a safe backend (or reject). 2) Avoid terminating TLS in the egress proxy for model-api traffic — preserve client_hello. 3) Temporarily pin the ALB listener default certificate to model-api cert so fallback doesn't show wildcard to customers.

maria: Agreed. I'll open a PR with the HAProxy ACL change + e2e test matrix (SNI present, SNI empty, trailing dot variants). Will also coordinate with certs team for listener default switch.

jon: One more thing — add a datapoint in tracing for "sni_present" boolean at edge so we can alert sooner.

maria: on it. Thanks all.

patrick: adding postmortem label. :thumbsup:
